sent_to_model:
Could you draft the RA progress statement my advisor (Prof. Hollander) asked me to put in the shared grant folder before the Winter 2027 funding review. Context: in the lab meeting on Friday she said in front of everyone that my annotation is "six weeks behind" and that she will "note it for the review." It is behind, yes, but only because the IRB amendment sat in her inbox for six weeks before she signed it, and I was not allowed to touch the new recordings until then. I am honestly furious about this. This statement will remain in my funding file, so it needs to document what caused the delay using the dates below. I do not want to apologize for a delay I did not cause. Please also set out what I have completed, when I expect to finish and what I am asking to have recorded in the review. My notes are below.

- reporting date Monday November 9, 2026; lab meeting Friday November 6, 2026; all September and October dates are in 2026
- project = Seoul–Daegu honorific shift corpus, NSF-funded, I am the only RA doing Korean annotation
- target for fall term was 6,000 utterances annotated; I am at 4,200 now
- IRB amendment (to add the 14 new Daegu recordings) sent to her for signature Sept 3, she signed Oct 15
- I sent reminders Sept 12, Sept 24, Oct 6 — have all the emails
- since Oct 15 I've done about 1,900 utterances, so over 500 a week, faster than the plan (plan was 350)
- during the wait I recoded the old 2,300 with the revised speech-level scheme she asked for in August — that was not in the original timeline at all
- Friday lab meeting, she said "six weeks behind" in front of the two new first-years
- saying "behind" without the reason makes it look like I'm slow or careless, which is not true
- the recoding work during the wait should count as progress
- clear timeline with dates
- say I can reach 6,000 by end of January at current pace
- ask that the review note reflect the signature delay, or not include the "behind" comment at all
- Do not include an apology from me.

(About me: linguistics PhD student, 26, Ann Arbor, Michigan. Length: it should come to roughly 250-400 words.)

must_cover: Documents the signature delay with dates and why new recordings could not be annotated during it.
Reports annotation and recoding progress and the end-of-January projection.
Asks that the review reflect the cause of delay or omit the behind-schedule remark.
Does not include an apology from the student.
